hypothesis: Oceanic islands lack Palaeozoic and Mesozoic rocks, so ocean basins and continents have kept their positions since the Silurian.
pass_criterion: Fewer than 5% of mapped units on genuinely oceanic islands (volcanic origin, not continental fragments) have Palaeozoic or Mesozoic ages, and no Palaeozoic unit is found.
fail_criterion: At least 20% of oceanic-island units are Mesozoic or older, or any Palaeozoic unit is found on a verified oceanic island.
interpretation: 'Secondary' means Mesozoic. Oceanic islands are defined as never-attached volcanic islands. Modern plate tectonics shows ocean floor is Jurassic or younger, so the stated inference about fixed oceans is expected to fail even if the island observation holds.

dataset.name: Macrostrat
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides geologic map polygons and rock units with numeric ages via an API, so island unit ages can be tallied.
